segments.t: While Chef Barinov begs through the door for his phone, Kristina corners Max in the dining room and makes it clear she always gets what she wants in her own restaurant. When Max says she can fire him, she threatens to fire Kostya instead unless Max comes to her after work.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'At least give me back my phone!' Max pushes back at once around Nastya, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
'As long as you keep hitting on me.' Nastya counters smoothly before Max and puts the emphasis on "pristavat" ("to pester, to harass") in the middle of the talk.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
'Maksim, I always get what I want.' Opening up plainly to Max, the "-sya" ending on "dobivayus" ("am courting") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'Especially in my own restaurant.' Max replies honestly in this moment, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'But you do not own the people.' Touching on the people with Max, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'You can even fire me if you want.' Cutting in promptly in the exchange, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Why fire you?' Max asks wryly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
'Well, or fire your friend Kostya.' Pointing to the guest to Max, Nastya leans on "gostya" ("guest, visitor", a form of "gost") to give the remark its edge.
'And here is why.' Turning dryly at once, Kristina links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'I am waiting for you after work.' Max pushes back openly during the talk, making his position completely clear.
'Here is the thing.' Addressing the matter on the spot, Nastya brings in "delo" ("matter") to make the meaning unmistakable.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?
'Could you possibly give me yours?' Jumping in frankly beside Max, Kristina keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Max purely through rising pitch.
'Not a chance.' Max opens up pointedly without holding back, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
Пока вы будете ко мне приставать.
Максим, я всегда добиваюсь того, чего хочу.
Не могла бы ты мне дать свой?

That wraps up this scene as in the dining room, Kristina corners Max and threatens to fire him or his friend Kostya over a broken bottle of vintage wine unless Max meets her after work. See you next time!
